newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch ban pig breeding in swine fever area.
newsitem.headline: Dutch ban pig breeding in swine fever area.

text.p: The Dutch farm ministry said on Monday it intended to impose a ban on pig breeding in an area at the heart of a swine fever outbreak in the south of the country.
The latest move to control the epidemic comes as the total number of cases has climbed to 225 and is showing little sign of coming under control.
A ministry spokesman said the ban would cover several hundred farms with around 50,000 sows in total.
"It will cover the centre of the area where swine fever started in February," the spokesman said.

The area -- a 10-kilometre radius around the village of Venhorst in the province of Brabant -- lies at the heart of a large pig-breeding district in which the transport of livestock and manure has already been banned.
Last week, Farm Minister Jozias van Aartsen said the total number of swine fever cases could rise to 300 before peaking.
In a letter to the Dutch parliament on Monday, Van Aartsen said the ban would come into force on June 3 and last for at least four months.

Some two million pigs have now been slaughtered -- more than 10 percent of the Netherlands' total 14 million pig population -- in an attempt to control the outbreak. The cost to farmers has been estimated by Van Aartsen at more than one billion guilders.
But the farmers have been compensated for much of this cost by the European Union.

Many of the Netherlands' key trading partners, including the United States, have halted imports of Dutch pigs and pork meat because of fears over the disease, which is highly contagious to animals but harmless to humans.

The Dutch government is pinning its hopes on a new type of vaccine, which it says will make the segregation of infected animals easier to detect. It hopes to have this so-called 'marker vaccine' in use by early next year.
